newsitem.title: USA: Court bars U.S. prosecution of pro-marijuana doctors.
newsitem.headline: Court bars U.S. prosecution of pro-marijuana doctors.

text.p: A U.S. judge issued a temporary restraining order on Friday blocking the federal government from prosecuting doctors who recommend marijuana to their sick patients.

U.S. District Judge Fern Smith in San Francisco also ordered the government and the plaintiffs, a group of physicians and patients advocating medical marijuana, to start negotiations to settle their dispute.

At issue is California's Proposition 215, approved by voters last November, which makes it legal under state law for sick people to grow and possess marijuana for medical use when recommended by a doctor.
The federal government, however, said it would prosecute or revoke the licenses of doctors who recommend marijuana to their patients under the California measure.

A group of California doctors, sick patients, medical associations and the American Civil Liberties Union filed suit asking the court to issue an order blocking the federal government from prosecuting any doctors.

Smith issued her temporary restraining order after the government's attorney said it would not hold off prosecuting doctors during the settlement negotiations as the judge had requested. The order takes effect immediately and will last until a settlement is reached, the judge said.
